The '''2019–20 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Arizona]] during the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team was led by 11th-year head coach [[Sean Miller]] and played their home games at [[McKale Center]] in [[Tucson, Arizona]] as members of the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12 Conference]]. They finished the season 21–11, 10–8 in [[2018–19 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12 play]] to finish in tie for fifth place. They received the No. 5 seed in the [[2020 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|2019 Pac-12 tournament]], where they defeated [[2019–20 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]] in the first round and were set to take on [[2019–20 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC]] in the quarterfinals before the remainder of the Pac-12 Tournament was cancelled amid the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]].

==Previous season==
The [[2018–19 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Wildcats]] finished the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19 season]] 17–15, 8–10 in [[2018–19 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12 play]] to finish in three-way tie for 6th place. They received the 9-seed in the [[2019 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|2019 Pac-12 tournament]], where they lost to 8-seed [[2018–19 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC]] in the first round, 78–65.

===2019 recruiting class===
[[Nico Mannion]], originally from [[Siena]], [[Italy]], was originally a part of the 2020 recruiting class, but [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] to the 2019 class in July 2018. He verbally committed to Arizona on September 14, 2018, over [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]]. Mannion is a consensus five-star prospect out of [[Pinnacle High School|Pinnacle HS]] in [[Phoenix, Arizona]].

[[Christian Koloko]], originally from [[Douala]], [[Cameroon]], was the second commitment in the Arizona class. He committed to Arizona on September 23, 2018, over [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]], [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]], and [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]]. He is a consensus four-star prospect out of [[Sierra Canyon School]] in [[Chatsworth, California]].

[[Josh Green (basketball)|Josh Green]], originally from [[Sydney]], [[New South Wales]], [[Australia]] was the third commitment in the Arizona's 2019 recruiting class. He verbally committed to Arizona on October 4, 2018, over [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] and [[UNLV Rebels men's basketball|UNLV]]. Green is a consensus five-star prospect out of [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]].

[[Zeke Nnaji]], originally from [[Lakeville, Minnesota|Lakeville, MN]] was the fifth commitment in the Arizona's 2019 recruiting class. He verbally committed to Arizona on November 23, 2018, over [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], North Carolina, Kansas and [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]]. Nnaji is a consensus four-star prospect out of [[Hopkins High School]] in [[Minnetonka, Minnesota]].

===2020 recruiting class===
[[Dalen Terry]], originally from [[Phoenix, Arizona|Phoenix]], [[Arizona]], was the first commit of the 2020 recruiting class.  He verbally committed to Arizona on July 23, 2019, over rival [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]], [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]], [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]], [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] and [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]]. Terry a consensus four-star prospect out of Hillcrest Prep in [[Phoenix, Arizona]].

[[Bennedict Mathurin]], originally from [[Montreal]], [[Canada]] was the second commitment of the 2020 recruiting class. He verbally committed to Arizona on January 15, 2020, over [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]] & [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]].  Mathurin was a consensus four-star prospect out of the NBA Academy Latin America.

[[Kerr Kriisa]], originally from [[Tartu]], [[Estonia]], was the third commitment of the 2020 recruiting class. He verbally committed to Arizona on April 18, 2020, over [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]], [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] & [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]]. Kriisa a consensus four-star prospect out of [[BC Prienai]] in [[Prienai]], [[Lithuania]].

Daniel Batcho, originally from [[Chatenay-Malabry]], [[France]], was the fourth commitment in the Arizona class. He committed to Arizona on April 23, 2020, over Arizona State, [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]], [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]] & [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]]. He is a consensus four-star prospect out of [[Centre Fédéral de Basket-ball]] in [[Paris, France]].

Tibet Gorener, originally from [[Şişli]], [[Turkey]], was the fifth commitment in the Arizona class.  He committed to Arizona on April 28, 2020, over [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]], Creighton, [[UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball|UC Santa Barbara]] & [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]]. He is consensus four-star out of [[Lutheran High School of Orange County|Orange Lutheran HS]] in [[Orange, California]].

[[Ąžuolas Tubelis]], originally from [[Lithuania]], was the sixth commitment in the Arizona class. He committed to Arizona on May 27, 2020. He is currently a four-star prospect out of [[Rytas Vilnius]] in Lithuania.

Tautvilas Tubelis, originally from [[Lithuania]], was the seventh commitment in the Arizona class. He committed to Arizona on May 27, 2020. He is currently an unranked prospect out of [[Rytas Vilnius]] in Lithuania.

==Schedule and results==
The Wildcats opponents were finalized in the summer and dates and times will be finalized in the fall. Arizona will host opponents [[Chico State University|Chico State]] (exhibition game), [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]], [[Long Beach State 49ers men's basketball|Long Beach State]], [[New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball|New Mexico State]], [[Northern Arizona Lumberjacks men's basketball|Northern Arizona]], [[Omaha Mavericks men's basketball|Omaha]], [[San Jose State Spartans men's basketball|San Jose State]], and [[South Dakota State Jackrabbits men's basketball|South Dakota State]] at [[McKale Center]] in [[Tucson, Arizona|Tucson, AZ]]. Arizona will participate in the 2019 [[Wooden Legacy]] in [[Anaheim, California|Anaheim, CA]] with six of the following potential opponents including ([[College of Charleston Cougars men's basketball|College of Charleston]], [[Pepperdine Waves men's basketball|Pepperdine]], [[Penn Quakers men's basketball|Penn]], [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]], [[UCF Knights men's basketball|UCF]], or [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]]). The Wildcats will also play in a neutral-site game against [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] at the new [[Chase Center]] in [[San Francisco|San Francisco, CA]] in the Naismith Memorial Hall of Fame Game. Arizona played only one true road game against [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] at [[Ferrell Center]] in [[Waco, Texas|Waco, TX]].

In the unbalanced 18-game Pac-12 schedule, Arizona did not play the two Rocky Mountain schools on the road ([[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]] and [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]]) or the two Northern California schools at home ([[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]] and [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]]).
